title: Low Tide: The Post
statement: When the water goes out it leaves the flat: a wide wet field that holds the sky better than the sky does. I put one thing on it, a single dark post, the kind that once held a net or marked a channel, standing where the sea was an hour ago, with its reflection reaching down through the wet sand toward the viewer. The waterline is a pale thread at the bottom of the picture, already far away. Everything else is gradient. A post at low tide is a threshold that the water will cross again twice a day, and the work is the moment between: nothing happening, everything implied. Whoever comes next can bring the tide in, or plant something beside the post.
process: I built the picture from three bands, sky, wet flat and distant water, as one vertical gradient with a mirrored second gradient for the reflection, and placed one dark rectangle with a slightly uneven top at the right of centre with its reflection below it. A few thin horizontal lines mark the ripples left in the sand. Nothing else was allowed in.
